summary: Chumphon Airport is a regional airport serving Chumphon Province in southern Thailand, located a short distance east of the provincial capital. It functions as a key air gateway for travelers heading to the Gulf of Thailand islands, particularly Ko Tao, and is operated by the Thai Department of Airports. The facility handles a modest volume of domestic traffic, primarily connecting Bangkok with this strategic southern transit point.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights at Chumphon Airport?
A: Nok Air and Thai AirAsia provide scheduled service, primarily connecting Chumphon with Bangkok (Don Mueang).

Q: How do I get from Chumphon Airport to the ferry pier for Ko Tao?
A: Shared minivans and taxis are available at the terminal and can take you to the Lomprayah or Songserm piers in about 45–60 minutes.

Q: How far is the airport from Chumphon city center?
A: The airport is roughly 10–12 km east of the town, with a typical drive taking around 20 minutes.

Q: Is there overnight accommodation near the airport?
A: A few small guesthouses and hotels are located in nearby areas, but most travelers stay in Chumphon town or head directly to ferry connections.
transport_tips: Pre-booking a combined minivan-plus-ferry transfer to Ko Tao through your accommodation or online is often the most convenient option, as it covers both the airport and pier legs. Taxis are available curbside but typically cost more than shared minivans. If heading to Chumphon town, motorcycles and tuk-tuks can be arranged in advance for budget-friendly transport.
local_tip: If you're connecting onward to Ko Tao, check ferry departure times before booking your flight—late morning arrivals align best with the main ferry schedules, and you can often complete the entire journey from Bangkok to Ko Tao in a single day.
